programme.title: Parcours C1 — 50 h
programme.subtitle: Maîtriser les communications professionnelles complexes et nuancées
programme.public_target: Cadres et professionnels de la communication, du marketing, de la négociation, de la finance ou de l'assistanat de direction.
programme.prerequisites: Niveau B2 estimé au positionnement. Équipement : ordinateur, micro, casque, connexion stable.
objectives: Mener une communication professionnelle stratégique, nuancée et adaptée à l'interlocuteur (C3).
Comprendre un discours étendu, implicite et idiomatique (C1).
Analyser des documents longs et complexes, attitudes et opinions implicites comprises (C2).
Argumenter, négocier et prendre la parole sans hésitation (C3).
Rédiger des rapports et écrits professionnels avancés d'au moins 200 mots en 30 minutes (C4).
programme.modalities: Formation ouverte et à distance (FOAD) : e-learning asynchrone sur la plateforme (leçons, audio, exercices auto-corrigés, studio oral, atelier d'écriture) et classes virtuelles synchrones avec le formateur.
programme.accompaniment: Formateur référent joignable par la messagerie de la plateforme (réponse sous 48 h ouvrées), rendez-vous individuels réservables dans l'agenda, assistance technique par messagerie (catégorie « support technique »).
programme.means: Plateforme LMS accessible 24 h/24, ressources audio et PDF téléchargeables, formateur anglophone qualifié (CV et compétences tenus à jour dans la plateforme).
programme.evaluation: Positionnement d'entrée ; exercices auto-corrigés et productions corrigées par le formateur ; quiz de fin de module (seuil 70 %) ; simulation d'entraînement aux 4 compétences ; évaluation finale interne ; questionnaires de satisfaction à chaud et à froid. Passage de la certification VTest sur la plateforme officielle d'ExAssess.
programme.accessibility: Formation accessible aux personnes en situation de handicap : demande d'aménagement confidentielle dès la candidature, analysée par le référent handicap (police agrandie, contrastes, temps majorés en entraînement, sous-titres et transcriptions). Les aménagements de l'examen officiel relèvent du certificateur.

objectifs: À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de reformuler un même message pour trois interlocuteurs différents (direction, client, partenaire) en adaptant l'angle, le registre et la phrase d'ouverture, sans hésitation notable.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de présenter une recommandation en 90 à 120 secondes en utilisant au moins deux procédés de cadrage (gain/perte, ancrage, contraste) et une structure explicite.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'annoncer une mauvaise nouvelle ou de tenir une déclaration de crise en reconnaissant les faits, en exprimant l'empathie et en annonçant des actions datées, sans minimiser ni spéculer.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de raconter une histoire d'entreprise structurée (situation, tension, tournant, résultat, message) en 90 secondes, avec au moins un chiffre concret.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de répondre à une question imprévue en 60 à 90 secondes en appliquant une structure d'improvisation (PREP ou passé-présent-futur) et des expressions pour gagner du temps.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'identifier et d'employer au moins dix expressions idiomatiques et procédés d'atténuation propres au discours professionnel de niveau C1.

modules.titre: Compréhension orale et nuances du discours
objectifs: À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'identifier l'intention réelle d'un locuteur (refus, réserve, critique, concession) derrière une formulation indirecte, avec au moins 8 réponses justes sur 10.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'interpréter correctement l'ironie, l'euphémisme et l'understatement en évaluant le degré réel d'un problème évoqué.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de paraphraser en anglais standard au moins 30 idiomes et phrasal verbs fréquents dans les réunions, négociations et communications financières.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'identifier la problématique d'un débat entre trois ou quatre intervenants, la position de chacun et la décision finale.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'extraire d'une keynote, d'une conférence de résultats ou d'un podcast la thèse principale et au moins trois données chiffrées exactes, quel que soit l'accent du locuteur.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de répondre correctement à au moins 75 % des questions portant sur des textes professionnels de 300 à 500 mots (rapports, tribunes, contrats, politiques, courriels, rapports d'audit), dans l'ordre du texte.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de qualifier l'attitude d'un auteur (prudence, scepticisme, ironie, autocritique, défense) en citant au moins deux indices textuels.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de restituer le sens implicite d'au moins cinq procédés (litote, euphémisme, concession, verbe introducteur, fausse excuse) dans un document professionnel.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de distinguer obligation, faculté, condition et exception dans une clause contractuelle ou une politique interne (shall, may, subject to, provided that, notwithstanding, are encouraged to).
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de comparer deux ou trois sources sur un même sujet et d'identifier au moins une convergence, une divergence et une omission.
À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de traiter un document complexe de 400 mots et ses questions en 9 minutes environ.

modules.titre: Argumentation, négociation et prise de parole
objectifs: À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de défendre oralement, en 90 à 120 secondes, une thèse délimitée appuyée sur au moins deux preuves et une réfutation anticipée, sans hésitation notable.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de mener une négociation de 12 minutes en explorant les intérêts de l'autre partie et en formulant des concessions exclusivement conditionnelles, jusqu'à un accord récapitulé sur au moins trois variables.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de présenter un pitch de 2 minutes en six étapes et des résultats chiffrés en annonçant d'abord le message clé et en décrivant les évolutions avec précision.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'ouvrir et de conduire une revue de projet en précisant l'objectif, le déroulement et les attendus de chaque participant, puis d'en récapituler les décisions (qui, quoi, quand).

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de répondre en moins de 90 secondes à une question hostile (fausse prémisse, faux dilemme, question multiple) sans l'éluder ni perdre son sang-froid, et de modérer un débat de manière impartiale.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger en 30 minutes un rapport de recommandation d'au moins 200 mots comportant objet, constats chiffrés, options évaluées, recommandation justifiée et prochaines étapes.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de condenser un document long en un executive summary autonome qui énonce la conclusion, les trois constats principaux et la décision attendue dans le premier tiers du texte.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger un cahier des charges ou un appel d'offres distinguant exigences obligatoires (shall / must) et souhaitables (should), avec critères d'évaluation et calendrier.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de défendre une position argumentée dans une note de position ou un texte de communication commerciale, en intégrant et en réfutant au moins une objection.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger un email à fort enjeu (escalade, excuses institutionnelles) qui reconnaît le problème sans aveu de responsabilité excessif et engage des actions datées.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger un document préparatoire à une réunion, une revue de projet ou un retour d'expérience présentant objectifs, thèmes abordés et attendus, de façon à fournir un ordre du jour précis aux participants.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'employer correctement dans un même texte au moins trois procédés de style C1 (inversion, nominalisation, cohésion par reprise lexicale ou démonstratif + nom) et de supprimer le jargon inutile.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de répondre en temps limité à deux séries complètes d'activités d'écoute de niveau C1 (déclarations, dialogues courts et longs, monologues, réponse construite) avec au moins 75 % de bonnes réponses, en repérant attitudes implicites et changements de position.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable d'analyser huit textes longs (emails, rapports, articles, comptes rendus) et d'y identifier opinions déclarées ou implicites, réserves et conséquences, avec au moins 75 % de bonnes réponses en moins de 40 minutes par série.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de réaliser les treize activités d'une simulation orale (3 lectures, 6 répétitions, 4 questions ouvertes de 45 à 120 secondes) en utilisant au moins 85 % du temps de parole et en structurant chaque réponse ouverte.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de rédiger en 30 minutes deux textes argumentés de plus de 200 mots, puis de présenter et formaliser par écrit la gestion d'une crise fournisseur à partir de sources orales et écrites.

À l'issue du module, l'apprenant est capable de comparer ses résultats internes aux critères C1 du référentiel et de formuler un plan de préparation au passage comportant au moins trois objectifs mesurables et datés.

competences: C1 — Écouter et comprendre un ensemble d'énoncés, de dialogues et de monologues en anglais afin de repérer, distinguer, identifier, sélectionner et apprécier des informations qui permettent de valider le degré de compréhension de la langue anglaise parlée nécessaire dans un contexte professionnel.

C2 — Comprendre et analyser un ensemble de textes, emails et articles en anglais afin de repérer, distinguer, identifier, sélectionner et apprécier des informations qui permettent de répondre à des questions avec précision dans un contexte professionnel.
C3 — S'exprimer et communiquer à l'oral en anglais afin d'apprécier les aptitudes à échanger, décrire, formuler, argumenter sur un ensemble de sujets dans un contexte professionnel.

C4 — Rédiger en anglais avec un vocabulaire et des tournures grammaticales appropriées afin de mesurer les aptitudes à écrire, décrire, formuler, questionner, argumenter, structurer ses idées sur un sujet donné dans un contexte professionnel.

syntheseHtml:
• Parcours C1 (50 h) préparant au VTest Business English – 4 Skills (RS6905, Répertoire spécifique, certificateur EXASSESS, enregistrement du 28/11/2024 au 28/11/2027) ; le test est passé en ligne sur la plateforme VTest, l'organisme assure la préparation.
• Les 4 compétences du référentiel sont travaillées : C1 — Écouter et comprendre un ensemble d'énoncés, de dialogues et de monologues en anglais ; C2 — Comprendre et analyser un ensemble de textes, emails et articles en anglais ; C3 — S'exprimer et communiquer à l'oral en anglais ; C4 — Rédiger en anglais avec un vocabulaire et des tournures grammaticales appropriées.
• 6 modules (61 leçons) : cours, langue clé, vocabulaire, dialogues, exercices auto-corrigés, studio oral et atelier d'écriture corrigés par le formateur, quiz de validation à 70 %.
• Le niveau A2 du CECRL est le minimum requis pour valider la certification : le test de positionnement d'entrée oriente vers le parcours adapté.

• Niveau de départ fixé par le test de positionnement ; le parcours peut être complété par les leçons du niveau inférieur ou supérieur.
• Rythme libre en e-learning, réécoute des audios et reprise des exercices ; classes virtuelles pour l'oral.
• Transcriptions et traductions disponibles pour chaque dialogue.
• Situation de handicap : le référent handicap étudie les aménagements (police agrandie, contrastes, temps majorés en entraînement, sous-titres) ; les aménagements de l'examen officiel relèvent du certificateur.
• Les sujets d'expression orale et écrite peuvent être rapprochés du poste du stagiaire.

qcmDebut.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Helen: So, Marcus, the engagement survey results for your department came back. Overall they're decent, but one thing stood out: people feel decisions are made without them. / Marcus: I'm a bit surprised, to be honest. I hold a team meeting every Monday. / Helen: Yes, and people mentioned that. The point seems to be that by the time something reaches the Monday meeting, it's already been settled. They feel informed rather than consulted. / Marcus: Fair enough. I suppose I've been trying to shield them from the endless back-and-forth with senior management. / Helen: That's understandable, and nobody doubts your intentions. But there may be a middle ground. You don't need to involve everyone in everything. / Marcus: What did you have in mind? / Helen: Perhaps flag upcoming decisions a week in advance and invite input on the ones that directly affect their work. And be explicit about which decisions are genuinely open and which aren't. / Marcus: I can see that working. Although I'd have to be careful it doesn't bog everything down. » — What is the real issue raised by the survey?
options: Staff feel they are told, not asked

qcmDebut.question: Document (article) : « When Green Claims Backfire For much of the past decade, sustainability messaging was treated by many companies as a low-risk, high-reward exercise. A carefully worded commitment to reach net zero by 2050 cost little, generated positive headlines, and was unlikely to be scrutinised until long after the executives who made it had moved on. That calculation is changing. Regulators in several jurisdictions now require environmental claims to be specific, substantiated and verifiable, and they have begun to fine firms that fall short. Meanwhile, activist investors and campaign groups have become adept at comparing public pledges with what companies actually disclose in their annual accounts, and are quick to publicise any gap. The result, somewhat paradoxically, has been a rise in what some analysts call greenhushing: companies that are making genuine progress choosing to say less about it, for fear that any imperfection in their data will be seized upon. A survey of 1,200 firms last year found that almost a quarter had deliberately scaled back their sustainability communications, even though their targets remained unchanged. Some observers welcome this as a healthy correction after years of exaggeration. Others are more concerned. If the companies doing the most are also saying the least, they argue, investors and consumers lose the very information they need to reward good performance, and the pressure on laggards to improve is correspondingly reduced. The challenge for regulators, then, is to deter misleading claims without discouraging honest ones. » — What does the writer suggest about sustainability claims in the past?
options: They carried little risk for those who made them
They were mainly made by small firms

Transcription de l'écoute : « Speaker: There's a tendency in these debates to treat productivity as if it were a single, easily measurable quantity. It isn't. / Speaker: When companies tell us remote staff are more productive, what they've usually measured is output on well-defined, individual tasks, which is precisely the kind of work that benefits from fewer interruptions. / Speaker: What those measures tend to miss is the slower, more diffuse stuff: the junior colleague who learns how to handle a difficult client by overhearing a call, or the idea that emerges from a conversation in the corridor. / Speaker: None of that shows up in this quarter's figures, but you'd be unwise to assume it doesn't show up eventually, usually in the form of a weaker talent pipeline. » — What is the speaker's criticism of claims about remote productivity?

qcmDebut.question: Document (email) : « From: Daniel Okoye, Operations Director To: Executive Committee Subject: Review of the warehouse automation pilot Colleagues, As requested, here is my assessment of the six-month automation pilot at our Tilbury warehouse, ahead of next week's decision on whether to extend it to our other three sites. The headline figures are, on the face of it, impressive: picking errors fell by 41 percent and throughput rose by 18 percent. I would caution, however, against reading too much into them. The pilot site was selected precisely because it had the most modern building and the most experienced workforce, and it received a level of support from the vendor's engineers that we cannot assume will be available, or affordable, at scale. More significantly, the projected payback period of three years rests on labour savings that have not yet materialised. Headcount at Tilbury is unchanged, partly because staff have been redeployed to supervise the robots, and partly because the system still requires manual intervention more often than the vendor anticipated. None of this is an argument for abandoning automation. I remain convinced that it is the right long-term direction. But I would recommend a more cautious next step: extending the pilot to one further site, ideally our oldest one at Corby, where conditions are least favourable. If the results hold there, we will have a far more reliable basis for a group-wide investment of this size. Daniel » — Why does Daniel question the headline figures?
options: They were calculated by the vendor
The pilot took place in unusually favourable conditions
They cover too short a period

Their client base complements ours almost perfectly, and the price is, if anything, on the low side. / Naomi: Which is precisely what makes me uneasy. Companies don't usually sell below value unless there's something they'd rather we didn't look at too closely. / Victor: Due diligence hasn't flagged anything major. There's the pending dispute with their former co-founder, but our lawyers think the exposure is limited. / Naomi: Limited according to whom, though? And based on what? / Victor: Our lawyers. Although, admittedly, they've only seen what Delmar chose to disclose. / Naomi: Then I'm not prepared to sign off on the current terms. I'm not saying we walk away, but I'd want part of the price held back until the dispute is settled. / Victor: An escrow arrangement. qcmDebut.question: Document (article) : « The Subscription Trap There was a time, not so long ago, when converting a product into a subscription was regarded as the closest thing in business to a free lunch. Recurring revenue was predictable, investors rewarded it with generous valuations, and customers, lulled by modest monthly fees, seemed scarcely to notice what they were paying in aggregate. That consensus is fraying. Churn rates across consumer subscription services have climbed steadily, and a growing share of customers now cancel and re-subscribe according to whatever they happen to want that month, a behaviour the industry has rather ruefully christened serial churning. What was meant to be a long-term relationship has, for many users, become a series of short-term transactions, with the added cost to the provider of re-acquiring the same customer several times a year. Business-to-business software, long assumed to be immune, is not faring much better. Finance departments under pressure to cut costs have started auditing the dozens of tools their companies subscribe to, often discovering licences that nobody has used in months. Vendors that once took renewals for granted are finding themselves in negotiations they had not prepared for. It would be premature to declare the model dead. For products that are genuinely used every day, a subscription remains a perfectly sensible arrangement for both sides. The difficulty lies with the many firms that adopted it not because it suited their product but because it suited their valuation. For them, the coming years are likely to involve some uncomfortable rethinking, and perhaps a quiet return to the old-fashioned practice of simply selling things. » — Why were subscriptions initially so attractive to companies?
options: They generated predictable income that investors rewarded

The reality is rather less obliging. / Commentator: A firm can relocate a factory in eighteen months; rebuilding the dense web of specialist suppliers, toolmakers and skilled technicians that once surrounded it can take a generation, if it happens at all. / Commentator: None of which is to dismiss the case for greater resilience. The pandemic exposed genuine vulnerabilities. But resilience and self-sufficiency are not the same thing. / Commentator: For most firms, the more realistic, and arguably more robust, strategy is diversification: spreading suppliers across several regions so that no single disruption can bring the whole operation to a halt. » — What point does the commentator make about reshoring?

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Charles Whitfield: That's certainly an interesting proposal, and we'll bear it in mind when we review our options next year. » — What does the speaker most probably mean?
options: He is enthusiastic and wants to start soon
He needs more information before deciding
He is politely declining the proposal for now
He has already chosen this proposal for next year
questions.explication: « an interesting proposal » et « we'll bear it in mind… next year » sont des formules typiques de refus poli en anglais britannique. Il ne demande aucune information supplémentaire.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Olivia Grant: That's certainly an interesting idea, and I'll bear it in mind, but I think we should stick with the current supplier for now. » — What is the speaker's real position?
options: She will seriously consider changing supplier
She wants more information before deciding
She is politely rejecting the suggestion
She agrees with the suggestion in principle
questions.explication: « interesting idea » et « I'll bear it in mind » sont des accords de façade ; « we should stick with the current supplier » révèle le refus. Elle ne demande pas d'informations supplémentaires (option 2).

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Martin Delacroix: Moving on to the rebranding. Hannah, I gather you've had second thoughts about the timing? / Hannah Lowe: Not about the rebrand itself; I'm still convinced it's overdue. What concerns me is launching it in the same quarter as the price increase. / Martin Delacroix: You think customers would connect the two? / Hannah Lowe: I think the press certainly would. 'New logo, higher prices' is a headline that writes itself, and it would undo a lot of the goodwill we're trying to build. / Gareth Pugh: With respect, Hannah, if we push the rebrand back, we lose the trade fair in May, and that's where most of our distributors will see it for the first time. / Hannah Lowe: That's a fair point. Could we unveil it to distributors at the fair, but hold the consumer launch until September? / Gareth Pugh: A soft launch to the trade first. I could live with that, provided the distributors are briefed not to share it publicly. / Martin Delacroix: Then let's go with a trade preview in May and a full launch in September. Gareth, could you draft the embargo note for the distributors? » — What is Hannah's main concern?
options: The rebrand is no longer necessary
The new logo has not been tested with customers
The rebrand may be linked to the price rise
The press has already criticised the price increase
questions.explication: « What concerns me is launching it in the same quarter as the price increase… 'New logo, higher prices' » : elle craint l'association des deux. Elle affirme au contraire que le changement d'image est nécessaire (« overdue »).

questions.question: Complétez chaque phrase avec le mot qui forme l'expression idiomatique correcte : « 1. The CFO finally _____ off on the revised budget yesterday. 2. If the pilot fails, it's back to the drawing board. 3. Can you give me a ballpark figure? It doesn't need to be exact. 4. The client keeps moving the goalposts, so we never know what they really want. 5. The merger fell through when the regulator raised objections. »
questions.explication: « to sign off on » = valider officiellement. « set off » signifie partir, sans rapport.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Anil Mehta, Project Lead, Bengaluru (Indian English): Jessica, we'd like to prepone the steering committee to Wednesday, if that's okay. The client audit has been moved up. / Jessica Moore, Programme Director, Atlanta (US English): Prepone, so you mean bring it forward? Wednesday works, but I'll need the deck by Tuesday noon, Eastern time. / Anil Mehta, Project Lead, Bengaluru (Indian English): Noon Eastern is nine thirty in the evening for us, so that should be fine. I'll share it by our end of day. / Jessica Moore, Programme Director, Atlanta (US English): Perfect. And can you loop in the risk team? They had questions last time. / Anil Mehta, Project Lead, Bengaluru (Indian English): Sure, I'll do the needful and add them to the invite. » — What does Anil want to do?
questions.explication: « prepone » (anglais indien) = avancer, reformulé par Jessica : « bring it forward ». L'option « later » correspond à postpone, le contraire.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Elena Rossi: I've seen the draft press release about the system outage. It says 'a small number of customers experienced minor delays'. / Hugh Bennett: That's what legal suggested. They want to keep it low-key. / Elena Rossi: I understand, but eleven thousand people couldn't access their accounts for six hours. If we call that minor, the story becomes our tone, not the outage. Let's give the real figure, apologise properly, and announce the compensation. / Hugh Bennett: Fair enough. I'll run your version past legal before lunch. » — What is Elena's main objection to the draft?
options: It minimises the scale of the incident
It was written without consulting legal
questions.explication: Elle reproche la minimisation (« small number… minor delays ») alors que onze mille clients ont été privés d'accès. Le juridique a bien été consulté : c'est lui qui a suggéré la formulation.

options: The press will focus on how the company frames the problem

questions.explication: Elle anticipe que la presse se focalisera sur le ton minimisant de l'entreprise plutôt que sur la panne elle-même. Elle ne propose pas un ton plus léger, au contraire.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Natalie Cho: I'd be comfortable signing off on the budget, provided the pilot is limited to two regions and we review the results in June. » — What is Natalie's position?
options: She rejects the budget until June
She approves the budget for all regions
She will decide after reviewing the results
She approves the budget under specific conditions
questions.explication: « I'd be comfortable…, provided… » exprime un accord conditionnel : deux régions et une revue en juin. Elle ne reporte pas sa décision : la revue de juin porte sur les résultats du pilote.

questions.question: Transcription de l'écoute : « Head of HR: I'm not saying the new policy is a bad idea, but I'd have liked to be consulted before it went out to six thousand people. » — What is the speaker's main feeling?
options: She disagrees completely with the policy.
She is annoyed about not being involved.
She is delighted with the policy.
She wants the policy sent to more people.
questions.explication: « I'd have liked to be consulted » : elle reproche de ne pas avoir été associée. « I'm not saying the new policy is a bad idea » exclut un désaccord total.

qcmCompetences.competence: C2 — Comprendre et analyser un ensemble de textes, emails et articles en anglais afin de repérer, distinguer, identifier, sélectionner et apprécier des informations qui permettent de répondre à des questions avec précision dans un contexte professionnel

questions.question: Document (email) : « From: Edward Pryce, Head of Procurement, Thornbury Group To: Lucia Marchetti, Account Manager, Vellora Packaging Subject: Revised proposal Dear Lucia, Thank you for the revised proposal, which arrived on Friday. I can see a great deal of work has gone into it, and the sustainability section in particular is a real step forward. I wonder, though, whether the pricing quite reflects the volumes we discussed in March. My colleagues in finance were, shall we say, a little surprised by the figure on page six. You may also wish to revisit the delivery schedule, as I'm not entirely sure a six-week lead time would sit comfortably with our retail calendar. None of this is insurmountable, of course, and we'd very much like to continue the conversation. Perhaps you could let me have your thoughts by the end of next week? Kind regards, Edward » — What does Edward actually mean by 'a little surprised by the figure on page six'?
options: Finance found the price slightly lower than expected
Finance needs more time to check the figure
Finance has noticed a typing error
Finance considers the price clearly too high
questions.explication: « shall we say, a little surprised » est un understatement typique : la surprise est en réalité forte et négative. Le contexte (volumes promis en mars) indique un prix jugé trop élevé.

questions.question: Document (report) : « Outlook and Principal Risks Ardent Biofoods N.V. — Annual Report 2025 (extract) Trading in the first weeks of the new financial year has been broadly in line with our expectations. Volumes in our plant-based dairy range continue to grow, albeit at a more measured pace than in 2024, when demand benefited from an exceptional promotional programme with two major retailers. We therefore expect revenue growth in 2026 to be in the mid-single digits, compared with 11% in the year under review. Input costs remain the most significant uncertainty. Oat and pea protein prices have stabilised since the summer, but they remain some 20% above their five-year average, and our hedging arrangements cover only the first half of the year. Should prices rise again in the autumn, we would seek to recover part of the increase through pricing, although our ability to do so will depend on the competitive environment in each market. We are not, at this stage, in a position to quantify the potential impact with any precision. The Board has also reviewed the risk associated with customer concentration. Our three largest customers accounted for 46% of revenue in 2025, up from 41% the previous year. These relationships are long-standing and, in our view, mutually beneficial; nonetheless, the loss or significant renegotiation of any one of them would have a material adverse effect on the Group's results. Diversifying our customer base, notably through the food-service channel, is one of the objectives of the strategy presented on page 14. Regarding regulation, proposed changes to labelling rules for plant-based products in two of our markets could require us to rename several items. We have engaged constructively with the authorities and believe that any changes can be managed within existing budgets, provided that a reasonable transition period is granted. Taking these factors into account, the Board remains cautiously optimistic. The fundamentals of the category are sound, our brands are well positioned, and our balance sheet gives us the flexibility to continue investing through the cycle. » — Why do the directors expect slower revenue growth in 2026?
options: Because consumers are losing interest in plant-based products.
Because 2025 benefited from a one-off promotion.
Because two major retailers have decided to stop selling the plant-based dairy range altogether.
Because the company has decided to raise its prices.
questions.explication: La croissance de l'année écoulée « benefited from an exceptional promotional programme » : la base de comparaison est donc gonflée. Les volumes continuent de croître, ce qui exclut la perte d'intérêt des consommateurs ; les distributeurs n'ont pas cessé de vendre la gamme.

questions.question: Document (report) : « B2B Buying Behaviour Survey 2026 — Key Findings Brightmoor Research Institute 1. Digital channels now dominate the early stages of purchasing Of the 1,850 procurement professionals surveyed, 71% said they complete more than half of their research before speaking to a supplier, compared with 58% in our 2023 survey. Buyers under 35 are the most independent: 84% of them prefer to shortlist suppliers without any contact with a sales representative. This does not, however, mean that sales teams have become irrelevant. Once a shortlist exists, two thirds of respondents still expect a detailed conversation with a specialist before committing to a contract worth more than €100,000. 2. Peer recommendations outweigh vendor content Asked which sources they trust most, respondents ranked recommendations from colleagues in other organisations first, followed by independent reviews. Vendor white papers and webinars came sixth out of eight. Interestingly, respondents who rated vendor content poorly were nevertheless frequent consumers of it, which suggests that such material is used for information gathering even when it is not trusted for decision-making. 3. Firms with structured buying committees report higher satisfaction Organisations in which purchases above a set threshold are reviewed by a cross-functional committee reported higher satisfaction with their suppliers than those in which decisions are taken by a single manager. We would caution against reading too much into this finding. Firms with formal committees tend to be larger and better resourced, and they may simply be in a stronger position to negotiate favourable terms. Our data do not allow us to isolate the effect of the committee itself. 4. Sustainability criteria are rising, but slowly Forty-three per cent of buyers said that environmental criteria were formally included in their supplier evaluations, up from 36% two years ago. However, only 12% reported that such criteria had been decisive in at least one contract award during the past year. The gap between policy and practice remains wide. Methodology note: the survey was conducted online in January and February 2026 across nine European countries. Results have been weighted by company size and sector. The margin of error for the full sample is approximately ±2.3 percentage points. » — According to section 1, what is true of buyers under 35?
options: They never speak to suppliers before signing a contract.
They make up 71% of the respondents.
They most often shortlist suppliers without salespeople.
They no longer expect any detailed conversation with a specialist, even for contracts above €100,000.
questions.explication: 84 % des moins de 35 ans préfèrent établir leur liste restreinte sans commercial. Le chiffre de 71 % concerne l'ensemble des répondants ; et le texte précise que deux tiers attendent encore un échange avant un gros contrat.

questions.question: Document (memo) : « MEMO To: All staff, Halden Logistics Group From: Marta Kowalczyk, Chief Compliance Officer Date: 2 February 2026 Subject: Updated Speak-Up Policy — what has changed and why Colleagues, Following the Board's annual review, our Speak-Up Policy has been updated, and the new version takes effect today. I would like to highlight the main changes and, just as importantly, explain the thinking behind them. First, you can now raise a concern through an independent hotline, operated by an external provider, by telephone or online, 24 hours a day and in eleven languages. You may choose to remain anonymous. Our existing channels — your line manager, HR and the Compliance team — remain available, and many of you will continue to prefer them. That is entirely your choice. Second, the policy now states explicitly that you do not need proof before speaking up. A reasonable belief that something is wrong is sufficient. If a concern raised in good faith turns out to be unfounded, you will not face any negative consequences. Deliberately false reports, on the other hand, will be treated as a disciplinary matter. Third, we have strengthened protection against retaliation. Any form of retaliation — including exclusion from meetings, unjustified changes to working hours or negative comments in performance reviews — will be treated as gross misconduct. Managers are expected to be particularly vigilant on this point, and all managers are required to complete a short training module by 31 March. Why these changes? Our annual staff survey showed that while most colleagues knew how to raise a concern, fewer than half felt confident that they could do so without any impact on their careers. Recent events in parts of our business have also shown that problems which are not raised early tend to become much more serious, and much more costly, later on. A culture in which people speak up is not a sign that something is wrong; it is one of the best indicators that things are being done right. The full policy is available on the intranet. If you have any questions, please contact me or any member of my team. Marta Kowalczyk » — What does the memo say about the existing reporting channels?
options: They have been replaced by the independent hotline.
They remain available alongside the new hotline.
They can now be used anonymously.
questions.explication: « Our existing channels… remain available, and many of you will continue to prefer them. » L'anonymat est mentionné pour la nouvelle ligne indépendante, pas pour les canaux internes.

qcmCompetences.competence: C3 — S'exprimer et communiquer à l'oral en anglais afin d'apprécier les aptitudes à échanger, décrire, formuler, argumenter sur un ensemble de sujets dans un contexte professionnel

questions.question: Choisissez la formule qui permet au président de conclure une discussion de comité : « So we're all agreed on a phased rollout. Let's _____ that as a decision, and Priya will report back in June. »
questions.explication: « to minute something » = le consigner au procès-verbal. « to table » signifie soumettre au débat (en anglais britannique), ce qui n'a pas de sens une fois la décision prise ; « to second » = appuyer une motion.

questions.question: Complétez ces formules de gestion du processus de négociation : « It feels as though we're going round in circles. Can we park the question of exclusivity for a moment and come back to it later? Let me check I've got the full _____: you need volume, and we need a March start. If we can't reach an agreement today, that's fine, but let's at least put what we've agreed in writing so there's no ambiguity. »
questions.explication: « the full picture » = la vision d'ensemble. « the full image » est un calque du français.

questions.question: Choisissez la formulation qui convient le mieux devant un comité de direction : « I'll _____: we won't meet the March deadline, and here's why. »
questions.explication: « to cut to the chase » = aller droit au but, idéal pour donner la conclusion d'abord. « cut it fine » signifie se laisser très peu de marge ; « cut both ways » = avoir des effets dans les deux sens.

questions.question: Complétez avec la structure d'emphase correcte : « _____ reduce our costs, but it would also improve delivery times. »
questions.explication: Après « Not only » en tête de phrase, l'auxiliaire précède le sujet : « Not only would it… ». « Not only it would » oublie l'inversion, erreur très fréquente.

questions.question: Choisissez la formulation la plus exacte dans une déclaration de crise, alors que l'enquête est en cours : « _____ that payment details were accessed. »
options: We have no evidence at this stage
questions.explication: Tant que l'enquête n'est pas close, on dose la certitude : « We have no evidence at this stage that… ». « We can guarantee » ou « It is impossible » engagent l'entreprise sur un fait non vérifié.

questions.question: Complétez l'expression idiomatique : « A six-month transition period should help to soften the _____ for the teams affected by the restructuring. »
questions.explication: La collocation figée est « to soften the blow » (amortir le choc). « soften the shock » ou « soften the hit » sont compréhensibles mais non idiomatiques.

questions.question: Choisissez la formulation qui exprime un désaccord de façon diplomatique : « _____, but I'm not sure the timing works for the Asian distributors. »
options: I can see where you're coming from
questions.explication: On reconnaît le point de vue de l'interlocuteur avant de nuancer. Les autres formules sont frontales, voire insultantes ; « with no respect » détourne « with the greatest respect ».

questions.question: Complétez avec l'expression qui permet de répondre honnêtement à une question imprévue : « I don't have the exact figures _____, but I'll send them to you by Friday. »

questions.question: Chaque phrase reprend une erreur fréquente relevée dans les rédactions du groupe. Choisissez la forme correcte, puis comparez votre réponse avec celle du formateur pendant la séance : « 1. We recommend that the committee approve the revised budget. 2. Costs rose _____ 9% last year, reaching €4.2 million. 3. Lumio and Pexa hold 28% and 19% of the market respectively. 4. Despite the high initial cost, the system pays for itself within two years. 5. We observed a significant increase in staff turnover. 6. The Provider shall respond to urgent requests within two hours (mandatory requirement). 7. The current situation is difficult, but we expect a recovery next year. 8. Far from simplifying the process, the proposal would increase administrative work. »
questions.explication: « rose by 9% » exprime l'écart ; « reaching €4.2 million » donne le niveau atteint (on aurait pu écrire « to €4.2 million »).

questions.question: Document (report) : « Learner's paragraph (market analysis, extract): The market of refurbished laptops is very big and it grows a lot, it was 620 million euros in 2025 and it has an important growth of 9%, this is amazing because the market of normal computers only grows of 2%. The actual leaders are Lumio, Pexa and Rendo, they have respectively 28, 19 and 11%. So there is a lot of place for new companies. Actually the public buyers must buy refurbished products because of a new law, so this is why the market grows. To conclude, we must absolutely go on this market. » — Which C4 criterion is most clearly met by this paragraph?
options: Precision and range of business vocabulary
Relevance to the task, with key figures
questions.explication: Le paragraphe reprend les chiffres clés et répond au sujet (taille, croissance, concurrence, moteur, conclusion). En revanche, la grammaire (grows of, an important growth), le vocabulaire (important, actual) et le registre (amazing, absolutely) sont fragiles.

We therefore recommend that the board _____ the relocation to the Saint-Priest site, provided that a detailed lease review is completed beforehand. Should the board approve this recommendation, the facilities team would begin negotiations in early May. The main risk, namely disruption during the move, could be mitigated by scheduling the transfer over two consecutive weekends. »
questions.explication: Après « recommend that », l'anglais écrit soutenu emploie le subjonctif, c'est-à-dire la base verbale sans -s : that the board approve. « approves » est une faute fréquente dans ce registre.

Questions to consider: what prevented earlier detection, and which safeguards worked as intended? Finance will _____ a proposal for an additional testing budget under item 4. »

questionsOuvertesDebut.question: Some companies are asking employees to return to the office full-time, while others are keeping remote work. What is your opinion on remote work? Give reasons and examples to support your view.
questionsOuvertesDebut.reponseAttendue: In my view, a hybrid model is clearly the most effective option, although I don't think there's a single answer for every company. On the one hand, remote work has real advantages. People save time on commuting, and for tasks that need concentration, such as writing a report or analysing data, working from home is often more productive. In my previous job, our team actually completed projects faster after we introduced two remote days a week. On the other hand, full-time remote work has hidden costs. New employees learn a lot simply by listening to experienced colleagues, and that's much harder over video calls. Creativity also suffers: many good ideas come from informal conversations that never happen online. That said, forcing everyone back to the office five days a week sends a message of mistrust and may push talented people to leave. So I'd argue that the best approach is to agree on shared office days for collaboration and leave the rest flexible. What matters is not where people work, but whether the organisation of work is clear and fair.

questionsOuvertesDebut.question: Describe a problem you had at work. What happened, what did you do to solve it, and what did you learn from it?
questionsOuvertesDebut.reponseAttendue: Last year, I was responsible for organising a training day for twenty new employees. Two days before the event, the trainer called me to say she was ill and couldn't come. At first I panicked, because the programme was already printed and everyone had booked the day. So I contacted two experienced colleagues, and they agreed to run the morning session. Then I asked the training company to send a replacement for the afternoon, and they found someone the same day. In the end, the feedback was very positive. What I learned is that you should always have a plan B, so now I keep a list of internal colleagues who can step in at short notice.

questionsOuvertesDebut.question: Your team is moving to a new office next month. Write an email to your colleagues to explain the move. Include: the date and the new address, what they need to do before the move, and what will be different in the new office. (Rappel : écrivez un courriel structuré à vos collègues, au moins 150 mots, en traitant les trois points demandés.)
questionsOuvertesDebut.reponseAttendue:
Subject: Our move to the new office on 14 November

Hi everyone,

As you know, our team is moving to a new office next month. I'd like to give you some practical information so that the move goes smoothly.

The move will take place on Friday 14 November. From Monday 17 November, we will work at 25 Harbour Street, on the fourth floor. The building is a ten-minute walk from Central Station, and there is a car park behind it.

Before the move, please do three things. First, clear your desk and put your personal items in the boxes that Facilities will deliver on 10 November. Second, label every box with your name and team. Finally, save all your files on the shared drive, because our computers will be reset.

There will also be some changes in the new office. We will not have fixed desks any more, so you will need to book a desk using the new app. However, there will be four meeting rooms instead of one, and a much bigger kitchen.

If you have any questions, please let me know.

Best regards,
Claire
