questionsOuvertesFin.question: Your company is considering a four-day working week for its head office staff. Argue either for or against introducing it as a trial, supporting your position with evidence and addressing the strongest objection.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: What I'd like to argue is that we should trial a four-day week at head office, for six months and for non-client-facing teams only. First, our engagement survey shows that workload and fatigue are now the main reasons people give for leaving, and replacing a manager costs us roughly half their annual salary. Which matters because even a modest drop in turnover would cover the cost of the trial. Second, several firms in our sector that have run similar pilots report stable or slightly higher output, largely because meetings get shorter and priorities get sharper. Now, you could argue that customers would find us harder to reach. That's a fair point, which is exactly why I'd exclude client-facing teams from the first phase. Admittedly, the evidence from other companies isn't conclusive. Even so, a time-limited, measured pilot carries very little risk. So what I'm proposing is a six-month trial, with output, absence and retention tracked monthly, and a go or no-go decision at the end.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: A board member claims that your company should stop all sponsorship of local sports clubs because 'it has no measurable return'. Present a reasoned counter-argument, using at least two pieces of evidence and showing where you agree with the board member.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: I take the point that sponsorship is harder to measure than, say, a digital campaign, and I agree that we shouldn't spend money we can't account for. But I'd question the premise that there's no measurable return. Last year, two thirds of our new apprentices told us they'd first heard of the company through a club we support, and in a tight labour market, that's a recruitment channel we'd otherwise have to pay agencies for. Secondly, our local sales team reports that sponsorship opens doors with small business owners who sit on those club committees. That's admittedly anecdotal, but it's consistent across three regions. So rather than stopping altogether, I'd suggest we keep the partnerships that clearly feed recruitment or sales, drop the ones that don't, and attach two or three simple indicators to each contract, such as applications received or meetings generated. In all likelihood, we'd end up spending less, but spending it far more deliberately. And if, after a year, the indicators show nothing, I'd be the first to recommend pulling out.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: In a meeting, a senior colleague states: 'Our customers don't care about sustainability; they only look at price.' You have survey data showing that 40% of your B2B customers now include environmental criteria in their tenders. Respond to your colleague tactfully but firmly.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: I can see where you're coming from, and I'd agree that price is still the deciding factor in most of our deals. That said, I'm not sure the data supports the idea that customers don't care about sustainability at all. In our last survey, forty per cent of our business customers told us they now include environmental criteria in their tenders, and that figure has roughly doubled in two years. So the way I'd put it is that sustainability may not win us a contract on its own, but it's increasingly what gets us onto the shortlist in the first place. Rather than debating it in the abstract, could we look at the last ten tenders we lost and check how many had environmental requirements we couldn't meet? That would give us a much clearer picture before we decide anything.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: You manage a conference venue. A corporate client insists on a 20% discount for their annual three-day event, which you cannot grant. Speak to the client: explore their interests, reframe the issue and propose a conditional solution that protects your margin.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: Thank you for being upfront about the twenty per cent. Before we talk figures, could you help me understand what's driving that number? Is it a reduction in your overall events budget, or is it more about the cost per delegate? And what would make this year's event a success from your side? If I've understood your colleague's email correctly, the real pressure is on the per-head cost, because attendance is likely to be lower this year. If that's the case, I think there's more room to work with than a straight discount. For example, if you could move the event from June to early May, which is a quieter period for us, we'd be in a position to reduce the room hire by around ten per cent. And provided that you confirm the booking for the next two years, we could include the evening reception at no extra charge, which would bring your cost per delegate down considerably. I can't go to twenty per cent on the current dates, but I'm confident we can find a package that works for both of us.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: You are buying cloud services for your company. At the end of a long meeting, the supplier's account manager says: 'Look, this is our final offer, and it's only valid until five o'clock today.' The offer is reasonable on price but the contract has no service level agreement. Respond.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: I appreciate you being clear, and I'll say straight away that the pricing is competitive; we're not far apart on that. But I'm not in a position to sign anything by five o'clock today, and to be honest, a deadline like that makes me more cautious rather than less. The real sticking point for us isn't price, it's the absence of a service level agreement. We're moving our customer-facing applications onto this platform, so an outage without any guaranteed response time or service credits is a risk my board simply won't accept. So here's what I'd suggest. If you can add a standard SLA, say ninety-nine point nine per cent availability with service credits, I'm confident we can sign this week at the price you've proposed. I'd much rather close this with you, so let's see whether your legal team can turn that around by Thursday.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: You sell industrial cleaning equipment. A prospect tells you: 'Your machine is 15% more expensive than your competitor's. Why should we pay more?' Make the case for your product without immediately offering a discount.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: That's a fair question, and you're right: on the purchase price alone, we're about fifteen per cent higher. But I'd encourage you to look at what the machine will actually cost you over its lifetime. Ours uses roughly thirty per cent less water and detergent, which, at your volumes, comes to around four thousand euros a year. It's also designed to run for ten years rather than six, and the maintenance contract is fixed for the first five, so you're not exposed to unexpected repair bills. And perhaps most importantly, downtime: our average response time for a breakdown is under twenty-four hours, which matters a great deal if a cleaning line stops during a production shift. So on total cost of ownership, we're actually cheaper by the end of year three. Could I ask what matters most to you here: the upfront budget, or the running costs? Because if the upfront figure is the real constraint, we could look at a leasing arrangement rather than touching the price itself.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: You are about to open a negotiation with a new partner. In about one minute, set the frame: thank your counterpart, propose how to structure the conversation, state your main priority without revealing your walk-away point, and ask an open question about their needs.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: Thanks very much for making the time today, Amara; I know your diary is full this month. I'd suggest we start by setting out what each of us needs from this agreement, then look at volumes and timing, and leave the detailed pricing until we have a clearer picture. From our side, the overriding priority is timing: the product has been approved and we're aiming for a launch in March, so a reliable start date matters more to us than almost anything else. We also want a partner we can grow with over several years, not just a one-off contract. So before we talk numbers, could you tell me what would make this partnership worthwhile from Pellworth's point of view, and whether there are any constraints on your side we should be aware of?

questionsOuvertesFin.question: Debrief your negotiation. Explain what outcome you reached (or why you reached none), describe one concession that worked well and one tactical mistake you made, and say what you would do differently next time.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: We reached an agreement on three of the four variables: a two-year contract, two million packs a year, and a guaranteed March start. The set-up fee wasn't waived, but it's spread across the unit price, which raises it by about two cents. The concession that worked best was offering a second year: I made it conditional on the March start, and that unlocked everything. My main mistake was revealing too early that March was critical. Once my partner knew that, she had a lot of leverage, and I think I paid for it on the unit price. Next time, I'd spend longer exploring her constraints before disclosing my own priorities, and I'd prepare a clearer ranking of my tradeables, because I hesitated when she asked about payment terms. One phrase I'll definitely reuse is 'Can we park that for a moment?'; it really took the tension out of the conversation.

questionsOuvertesFin.question: A high-performing team member asks you for a 12% pay rise. Your budget allows a maximum of 4% this year, but you are keen to keep her. Respond: acknowledge her contribution, explain the constraint honestly, and offer at least two concrete alternatives with a clear next step.
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: First of all, thank you for raising this directly, and let me say clearly that your request is justified. Since you took over the product data project, we've cut reporting time by half, and two other departments now rely on your dashboards. I'll be completely transparent about the constraint: this year, I can't go beyond four per cent on base salary, and I don't want to promise you something I can't deliver. But I don't think the conversation should stop there. Two things I can do. First, your role has clearly grown, so I'd like to put you forward for a regrade to senior analyst, which sits outside the annual budget and would bring your salary much closer to what you're asking. Second, I can add a performance bonus tied to the data platform launch, worth up to six per cent. I'll submit the regrade request to HR by the end of next week and give you their answer before the end of the month. Would that be a reasonable way forward?

questionsOuvertesFin.question: Pitch a new service or internal project (real or imagined) to an investment committee or to your company's executive board. Include a hook, the problem, your solution, the market or scope, evidence of traction, and a precise request (amount, use of funds, milestones).
questionsOuvertesFin.reponseAttendue: Last year, our field technicians spent an average of forty minutes a day looking for the right spare part or the right manual. Across three hundred technicians, that's the equivalent of twenty-five full-time jobs, lost every year. The tools we have today were designed for the office, not for someone standing on a ladder in a client's plant room. So we've built FieldMate, a voice-driven assistant that technicians can query hands-free, in their own language, and that pulls answers directly from our maintenance database. What this means in practice is simple: today, technicians search; with FieldMate, they ask. We ran a three-month pilot with forty technicians in the Lyon region. Search time fell by sixty per cent, first-time fix rates rose by nine points, and thirty-seven of the forty asked to keep the tool. We're now asking the board for four hundred and fifty thousand euros to roll it out to all three hundred technicians over the next twelve months: two thirds for integration and licences, one third for training. The first milestone is full coverage in France by June, and on our estimates, the project pays for itself in under eighteen months.

exercices.consigne:
Your team will deliver a client report two weeks late because a data provider changed its format. Explain the situation first to your managing director, then to the client's finance director.
Préparation 45 s, réponse orale de 90 s.
Critères : Ouvre chaque version par l'information essentielle (conclusion d'abord pour la direction, impact concret pour le client). ; Change d'angle de façon perceptible : risque et maîtrise interne d'un côté, conséquences pratiques et garanties de l'autre. ; Emploie au moins une phrase clivée et deux procédés d'atténuation ou de cadrage. ; Ne se justifie pas de manière défensive ; mentionne la cause une seule fois, factuellement. ; Parle de façon fluide pendant 75 à 90 secondes, sans pause longue ni recherche de mots..
exercices.reponseAttendue: First, to our managing director: the short version is that the Halden Mutual report will be two weeks late, and the risk is contained. Our data provider changed its file format without notice, which meant rebuilding two of our models. It's not the extra work that worries me so much as the client's board meeting on the twentieth, so I've already secured a slot to walk them through the preliminary figures beforehand. No impact on fees, and I'll confirm the final date by Friday. Now, to the client's finance director: I wanted to speak to you personally about the timing of the report. What this means for you in practical terms is that you'll receive the full version on the fourteenth rather than the first. However, you'll have the key indicators for your board in time, because we'll present them to you next Tuesday. I'd rather give you a date we can stand behind than one we'd have to revisit, and I'll keep you posted at every stage.

exercices.consigne:
Your company is considering whether to keep its annual client event in a luxury hotel or move it online. You are convinced it should remain in person, despite the higher cost. Make your case to the management committee.
Préparation 60 s, réponse orale de 120 s.
Critères : Pose un cadre explicite (gain/perte, investissement plutôt que coût, contraste) dès l'ouverture. ; Appuie l'argument sur au moins un chiffre ou un fait vérifiable plausible. ; Formule une concession réelle et revient à la thèse (Granted… That said…). ; Emploie au moins une structure d'emphase (inversion, phrase clivée ou question rhétorique). ; Termine par une demande précise et parle sans hésitation pendant 90 à 120 secondes..
exercices.reponseAttendue: I'd like to start by reframing the question. We tend to talk about the client event as a cost line of around ninety thousand euros. I'd suggest we look at it instead as the single most effective retention tool we have. Last year, eleven of the forty clients who attended in person signed new or extended contracts within three months, worth well over a million in combined revenue. Not only does the event deepen relationships, but it also gives our account teams something no video call can: unscheduled conversations over coffee, which is where most of our upsell opportunities actually come from. Granted, the hotel is expensive, and an online format would be cheaper and easier to organise. That said, we ran a webinar version in 2021 and attendance dropped by half, while follow-up meetings practically disappeared. So what's the real cost of saving ninety thousand? Potentially, a large share of next year's renewals. What I'm asking for today is approval to keep the in-person format, with a ten percent budget cut that I'll achieve by shortening the event to a single day.

exercices.consigne:
A journalist asks you: 'Your online banking app has been down for nine hours. Customers can't pay their bills. Isn't this simply the result of cutting your IT budget last year?'
Préparation 60 s, réponse orale de 90 s.
Critères : Répond d'abord brièvement à la question posée, sans « no comment » ni démenti non vérifié. ; Reconnaît l'impact pour les clients et présente des excuses sans formule administrative. ; Annonce des actions précises (faites et en cours) et un prochain point d'information daté. ; Utilise au moins deux formules de recentrage ou de dosage de la certitude (At this stage…, What I can tell you is…). ; Garde un ton calme et un débit maîtrisé pendant 75 à 90 secondes..
exercices.reponseAttendue: I understand why you're asking that, and it's a fair question. It would be wrong of me to speculate about the cause while our engineers are still investigating, but I can tell you that our IT investment has actually increased this year, and we'll share the full findings once we have them. What matters most right now is our customers. Many of them haven't been able to pay bills or move money since this morning, and that's simply not acceptable. We're sorry. Here's what we're doing. We've restored access to card payments and cash withdrawals, which are working normally. Our teams are working to bring the app back online, and we expect a partial restoration within the next three hours. In the meantime, anyone who incurs a late payment fee because of this outage will be reimbursed in full; they don't need to prove anything, they just need to contact us. We will give a further update at six o'clock this evening, and I'll be happy to take your questions again then.

exercices.consigne:
You manage a team of six. Your director has just refused the two promotions you had requested for your team members, citing a company-wide freeze. Break the news to one of the employees concerned, who has been expecting it.
Préparation 45 s, réponse orale de 90 s.
Critères : Annonce la décision clairement dans les 20 premières secondes, après un signal d'alerte bref. ; Donne la raison réelle sans se désolidariser de l'entreprise (pas de « It's not my decision »). ; Reconnaît l'impact et la déception de l'interlocuteur avec des formules sincères. ; Propose au moins une alternative concrète et une prochaine étape datée. ; Atténue la forme (modaux, passé de politesse) sans rendre la décision ambiguë ; débit posé pendant 75 à 90 secondes..
exercices.reponseAttendue: Thanks for coming in, Laura. I'm afraid I don't have the news you were hoping for, and I'd rather tell you face to face. The promotion we discussed won't go ahead this year. The company has frozen all promotions until the end of the financial year, and there are no exceptions, not even for the cases we put forward. I know how much you've invested in the Halloran account, and I realise this is a real disappointment, especially after the feedback you received in June. I want to be clear that this has nothing to do with your performance, which I've documented in writing. What I can do, however, is make sure you're first in line when the freeze is lifted in April: your file is ready and has already been endorsed by the director. In the meantime, I'd like you to lead the client review in January, which will give you visibility with the management committee. Why don't we sit down again next Tuesday, once you've had time to think it over, and agree on a development plan together?

exercices.consigne:
You are welcoming a group of new recruits to your company. Tell them a short story about a moment when things went wrong at work and what the team learned from it.
Préparation 60 s, réponse orale de 90 s.
Critères : Suit les cinq temps : situation, tension, tournant, résultat, message. ; Emploie au moins trois temps du passé différents (prétérit, past continuous, past perfect) de façon correcte. ; Utilise au moins un procédé de mise en relief (inversion, phrase clivée, discours direct ou présent de narration). ; Inclut au moins un détail concret ou chiffré et relie le message aux nouveaux arrivants. ; Raconte avec fluidité pendant 75 à 90 secondes en variant le rythme..
exercices.reponseAttendue: Let me tell you about my second week in this job, about six years ago. We were preparing the annual results presentation for our biggest shareholder, and I'd been asked to check the figures. The night before the meeting, I was going through the appendix one last time when I realised that a whole column had been copied from the previous year. Two hundred numbers, all wrong. Now, I was the newest person on the team, and the deck had already been approved by the finance director. Little did I know how she would react. I picked up the phone, my heart pounding, and said, 'I think we have a problem.' And she simply replied, 'Thank you. Let's fix it together.' We worked until two in the morning, and the presentation went ahead without a single error. It wasn't until much later that I understood what had happened that night: she'd made it safe for a junior colleague to raise a problem. So here's my message to you: if you spot something that doesn't look right, say so. Nobody here will ever blame you for asking.

exercices.consigne:
Off the top of your head: should companies allow employees to choose freely between working from home and working in the office?
Préparation 15 s, réponse orale de 60 s.
Critères : Reformule ou délimite la question dans la première phrase. ; Donne une position claire dans les 15 premières secondes, assortie d'une nuance. ; Appuie l'avis sur une raison et un exemple concret. ; Conclut en revenant explicitement à sa position. ; Parle 50 à 60 secondes sans remplissage vide ni longue pause..
exercices.reponseAttendue: So, if I understand the question correctly, it's about complete freedom of choice, rather than hybrid working in general. On balance, I'd say no, not entirely, although I'm strongly in favour of flexibility. The main reason is that some activities simply work better face to face: onboarding new staff, for instance, or creative workshops. In my previous company, we let everyone choose, and within a year our new recruits were taking twice as long to become autonomous, because nobody was around to answer their questions. So my take on it is this: give people a lot of freedom, but agree on two or three anchor days a week when the team is together.

exercices.consigne:
A senior manager stops you in the corridor and asks: 'How has your department's way of working changed over the last few years, and where do you see it going?'
Préparation 20 s, réponse orale de 90 s.
Critères : Organise la réponse en trois temps clairement signalés (A few years ago… Today… Going forward…). ; Emploie correctement le present perfect pour les évolutions et le futur ou des modaux pour les perspectives. ; Exprime au moins une opinion nuancée sur l'évolution décrite. ; Gère honnêtement une information manquante, le cas échéant. ; Termine par une phrase de clôture nette ; discours fluide pendant 75 à 90 secondes..
exercices.reponseAttendue: That's a big question, so let me take it in three steps. A few years ago, our accounts payable team was essentially processing paper invoices: we had around eight people keying in data, and closing the month took nearly two weeks. Since then, things have changed considerably. We've automated most of the data entry, and today the month-end close takes five working days. The team is the same size, but the work is very different: people now spend most of their time analysing exceptions and talking to suppliers rather than typing. I'd say that's been a genuinely positive change, although some colleagues found the transition hard, and I think we underestimated the training effort. Going forward, I expect AI tools to take over a good part of the exception handling too. I don't have the vendor's latest roadmap to hand, but my understanding is that a pilot could start next year. So, in short: less processing, more judgement, and that's where we'll need to invest in skills.

exercices.consigne:
During a video call, a senior partner from your company's Tokyo office proposes moving the launch of a joint product forward by two months. You believe this is unrealistic. He has spoken in front of his whole team. Respond.
Préparation 45 s, réponse orale de 90 s.
Critères : Reconnaît d'abord la proposition et ses mérites, sans formule creuse. ; Exprime le désaccord de façon dépersonnalisée (données, contraintes) et non frontale. ; Vérifie un point de compréhension par une question de reformulation. ; Propose une alternative qui permet à l'interlocuteur de préserver la face devant son équipe. ; Adopte un débit posé, des phrases claires et évite les idiomes trop locaux ; 75 à 90 secondes..
exercices.reponseAttendue: Thank you, Mr Sato, and thank you to your team for such a detailed plan. I fully understand the reasoning: an earlier launch would put us ahead of the competition before the year-end season, and that's a very real advantage. Just so I'm clear, are you proposing to move the whole launch forward, including the European markets, or mainly the Japanese one? I ask because, from our side, the regulatory approval in Europe is the main constraint. Our latest information suggests it won't be granted before late March, so a launch in January there would be difficult for us. Might it be worth considering a phased approach? We could launch in Japan in January, as your team suggests, and use those first eight weeks to gather customer feedback, which would strengthen the European launch in March. That way, we benefit from your team's timing and reduce the regulatory risk. Perhaps our project leads could look at this together this week and share a revised timeline on Friday?

exercices.consigne:
You are presenting to the executive committee of a mid-sized marketing agency. You recommend replacing the agency's three separate project-management tools with a single platform. Present your recommendation.
Préparation 60 s, réponse orale de 120 s.
Critères : Énonce la décision attendue dans la première phrase. ; Présente au moins deux options et justifie la recommandation par deux raisons, dont une chiffrée. ; Nomme le principal risque et la mesure qui le limite. ; Formule une demande précise (montant, calendrier, date de revue). ; S'exprime sans hésitation pendant 100 à 120 secondes, avec des structures d'emphase et de nuance de niveau C1..
exercices.reponseAttendue: Good morning. I'm here to ask for your approval to replace our three project-management tools with a single platform from the first of March. Let me explain why. At the moment, the creative team, the media team and account management each use a different system. In practice, that means project information is re-keyed two or three times, and our own time tracking shows it costs us around six hours per person per month. Across sixty staff, that's roughly the equivalent of two full-time salaries. We looked at three options: keeping the current set-up, connecting the existing tools through an integration layer, or moving to a single platform. The integration option looked attractive at first, but it would still leave us paying three licences and maintaining the connectors. That's why we recommend a single platform, which would also give clients a shared view of their projects, something two of our largest accounts have asked for. The main risk is adoption: people are attached to their tools. We'd mitigate that by migrating one team at a time, starting with account management, and by appointing a champion in each team. What I'm asking for today is a budget of forty-five thousand euros for the first year, covering licences and training, with a go/no-go review at the end of June based on time saved and client feedback.

exercices.consigne:
What do you think is the most overrated skill in business today, and why?
Préparation 15 s, réponse orale de 60 s.
Critères : Donne une position claire dès la première ou la deuxième phrase. ; Respecte la contrainte (une inversion correcte et l'idiome imposé, employés à bon escient). ; Justifie par une raison et un exemple concret, puis nuance l'avis. ; Termine par une phrase de clôture qui revient à la position initiale. ; Parle 50 à 60 secondes sans remplissage vide (um, er, you know, like)..
exercices.reponseAttendue: If I had to pick one, I'd say multitasking. It's often presented as an essential skill, but rarely does it deliver what people expect. The main reason is that switching between tasks has a cost: every time you jump from an email to a spreadsheet and back, you lose focus. In my team, we tried blocking two hours each morning with no meetings and no messages, and not only did the error rate in our reports fall, but people also left the office earlier. Having said that, I'd accept that responsiveness is a double-edged sword: clients do expect quick answers, so you can't disappear for a whole day. But on balance, I'm convinced: multitasking is the most overrated skill in business, and deep focus is the most underrated.

exerciceIntermediaire.contexte: Évaluation à mi-parcours (modules C1-M2 à C1-M4) : productions orales et écrites corrigées par le formateur avec les critères de chaque sujet.

questions.question:
Expression orale — C1-M4-L9-I1 (C1.2) — A panel member asks you: 'Your projections assume you'll triple your customer base in eighteen months. Isn't that wildly optimistic?' Answer the question.
Préparation 30 s, réponse orale de 60 s.
Critères : Réponse directe dès la première phrase (Answer). ; Justification par au moins un fait ou une donnée (Detail). ; Reconnaissance honnête de l'incertitude, sans affaiblir le propos. ; Retour au message clé ou à la demande en conclusion (Direction). ; Aucun préambule inutile ; débit fluide..
questions.reponseAttendue: It's ambitious, but I wouldn't call it wildly optimistic, and here's why. Over the last six months, we've grown by about seven per cent a month, almost entirely through referrals, without any paid marketing at all. Tripling in eighteen months requires roughly six and a half per cent a month, so we're actually assuming a slight slowdown. What could change that picture is our dependence on two distribution partners, and I fully accept that if one of them pulled out, we'd be looking at doubling rather than tripling. That's precisely why part of this round is earmarked for building our own sales team, so that by the end of next year, partners account for less than half of new customers. So yes, it's a stretch target, but it's grounded in what we're already delivering.

questions.question:
Expression orale — C1-M4-L10-I2 (C1.2) — You are chairing a project review. The launch of a new mobile app is four weeks late and the marketing and development teams blame each other. Open the meeting: state the purpose, explain how the review will run, set out exactly what you expect from each participant, and establish ground rules.
Préparation 60 s, réponse orale de 90 s.
Critères : Objectif énoncé en une phrase, orienté solution (et non recherche de coupable). ; Déroulé en étapes ordonnées, avec une indication de durée. ; Attendus précis par participant ou par équipe (qui apporte quoi, quelle décision en sortie). ; Au moins une règle de fonctionnement explicite. ; Ton ferme et apaisant ; formulations variées (I need…, could you…, I'd like…)..
questions.reponseAttendue: Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for making the time. I'm aware this has been a frustrating few weeks for both teams, so let me be clear about what today is for. The purpose of this review is to agree on a credible new launch date, not to decide whose fault the delay is. We'll take it in three stages. For the first fifteen minutes, we'll establish the facts: where each workstream is against the original plan. Then we'll spend about twenty minutes on causes, looking at handovers between marketing and development rather than at individuals. And we'll use the last twenty-five minutes for options and a decision. In terms of what I need from you: Sara, could you bring the current status of the app store submission and any outstanding bugs? Tom, I'd like the marketing team to tell us which campaign dates are fixed and which can still move. By the end of the hour, I need one agreed launch date and an owner for every remaining action. Two ground rules: we stick to facts and figures, and if a topic is outside today's scope, we'll note it and take it offline.

questions.question:
Expression orale — C1-M4-L11-I2 (C1.2) — You are the head of customer service at a telecom company. At a staff town hall, an employee asks: 'Isn't the new chatbot just a way to get rid of half of us without admitting it?' Answer the question.
Préparation 45 s, réponse orale de 75 s.
Critères : Reconnaissance de l'inquiétude sans valider la prémisse. ; Recadrage explicite de l'accusation implicite. ; Réponse factuelle et vérifiable (engagements, chiffres, calendrier). ; Retour au message clé (bridging) en conclusion. ; Aucune reprise des termes négatifs de la question ; ton calme et respectueux..
questions.reponseAttendue: Thank you for asking that so openly; I know a lot of people are wondering the same thing, and it's far better to discuss it here than in the corridor. I don't accept that there's a hidden agenda, and I'll be as specific as I can. The chatbot will handle simple requests, such as password resets and billing dates, which currently make up about a third of our calls. We've committed, in writing, to no compulsory redundancies in customer service as a result of this project. What will change is the nature of the work: fewer repetitive calls, and more of the complex cases that customers actually need a person for. Over the next six months, every adviser will be offered training in technical support or retention, and both of those teams are recruiting. And that's really the point of this change: to give you more interesting work, and to give customers faster answers. If anyone wants to see the commitment in writing, I'll share it with the whole team this afternoon.

questions.question:
Expression orale — C1-M4-L11-I3 (C1.2) — You are the CEO of a food company that has just recalled a batch of products. A journalist asks: 'How many people have been affected, who's responsible, and what will you do if regulators fine you?' Answer professionally.
Préparation 45 s, réponse orale de 75 s.
Critères : Signalement explicite de la question multiple et choix d'un ordre de traitement. ; Réponse factuelle sur la question prioritaire (santé des consommateurs). ; Refus argumenté de désigner un responsable prématurément. ; Refus de spéculer sur l'hypothèse, assorti d'une information utile. ; Retour au message (sécurité, transparence) ; sang-froid perceptible dans le débit..
questions.reponseAttendue: There are three questions there, and I'd like to start with the one that matters most, which is people's health. As of this morning, we've received eleven reports of mild illness, and as far as we know, nobody has needed hospital treatment. Anyone who bought the product can return it to any store for a full refund, and our helpline is open around the clock. On responsibility, I'm not going to point fingers before the investigation is complete; that wouldn't be fair, and it wouldn't help anyone. What I can tell you is that the problem has been traced to a single production line, which has been shut down, and an independent laboratory is reviewing our procedures. As for a possible fine, I'm not going to speculate on what regulators might decide. We're cooperating fully with them, and we'll publish the findings of the investigation. Our priority right now is simple: making sure every affected product is off the shelves and that this cannot happen again.

evaluationFinale.titre: Évaluation finale interne — 4 épreuves (C1 à C4) notées sur 20, au format d'entraînement du VTest

exercices.consigne:
Écoutez l'enregistrement (transcription réservée au formateur : Operations Director: Bringing in agency staff will get us through the peak, granted, but if we're still relying on them in March, we'll have to admit that the scheduling problem was never really fixed.), puis répondez.
1. What is the speaker's view of using agency staff?
A. It is the best long-term option for getting through the peak season
B. It should be stopped before the peak begins
C. It is a short-term fix that leaves the real problem unsolved
D. It has already solved the scheduling problem
exercices.reponseAttendue: 1. C — It is a short-term fix that leaves the real problem unsolved. « granted » concède l'utilité immédiate (passer le pic), puis « the scheduling problem was never really fixed » montre que ce n'est qu'un palliatif. L'option « already solved » est le piège : la locutrice dit précisément le contraire.

exercices.consigne:
Lisez le document, puis répondez.
From: Imogen Clarke, Head of Procurement, Brindlewood Foods
To: Marcus Hale, Account Director, Ostfield Logistics
Subject: Service levels under our current agreement

Dear Marcus,

Thank you for your call on Tuesday and for the candour with which you described the staffing difficulties at your Northampton hub. I appreciate that the past quarter has been exceptionally challenging for the whole sector, and I want to be clear that this email is not intended as a prelude to terminating our agreement.

That said, the figures speak for themselves. On-time delivery to our stores fell from 97 per cent in the first quarter to 88 per cent in the third, well below the 95 per cent threshold in our service-level agreement. More concerning than the headline figure is the pattern: almost all late deliveries involved chilled products, which have the shortest shelf life and the highest cost when wasted.

Under clause 9.2, we would be entitled to a service credit of roughly £64,000 for the quarter. I am prepared to waive half of that amount, on the condition that Ostfield presents a written recovery plan by 15 November, including named responsibilities and weekly reporting on chilled deliveries until performance is back above the threshold for two consecutive months.

I would also ask that you consider ring-fencing a dedicated team for our chilled volumes over the Christmas period. I recognise this has a cost, and I am open to discussing how it might be shared.

I look forward to your proposal.

Kind regards,
Imogen Clarke
1. What does Imogen make clear at the start of the email?
A. She intends to end the contract with Ostfield
B. She is not planning to cancel the agreement
C. She was unaware of the staffing problems
D. She blames the whole sector for the delays
2. According to Imogen, what is the most worrying aspect of the performance?
A. The overall drop in on-time deliveries to stores
B. The number of stores affected
C. The cost of the service credit
D. The concentration of delays on chilled products
3. What is Imogen's position on the cost of a dedicated team?
A. She is willing to negotiate a shared arrangement
B. She expects Ostfield to pay the full cost
C. She will pay for it if the recovery plan is accepted
D. She considers it unnecessary before Christmas
exercices.reponseAttendue:
1. B — She is not planning to cancel the agreement. « this email is not intended as a prelude to terminating our agreement » : elle ne compte pas résilier. Elle avait été informée des difficultés de personnel lors de l'appel de mardi, ce qui écarte la troisième option.
2. D — The concentration of delays on chilled products. « More concerning than the headline figure is the pattern: almost all late deliveries involved chilled products » : la concentration sur les produits frais. Le chiffre global (88 %) est explicitement jugé moins préoccupant.
3. A — She is willing to negotiate a shared arrangement. « I am open to discussing how it might be shared » : partage du coût négociable. Elle ne promet pas de payer seule, et ne lie pas ce point au plan de redressement.

exercices.consigne:
Present these half-year results to your management team: customer satisfaction score rose from 72 to 81; average response time fell from 9 hours to 4 hours; but the support department's costs were 12% over budget, mainly because of temporary staff hired during a system migration. Explain the figures, distinguish one-off from structural factors, and finish with next steps.
Préparation 60 s, réponse orale de 90 s.
Critères : Message clé annoncé en premier (bottom line up front). ; Évolutions décrites avec précision (by / to / from…to, verbes et adverbes variés). ; Distinction explicite entre facteur ponctuel et facteur durable. ; Dépassement budgétaire présenté avec transparence, sans euphémisme excessif. ; Conclusion sur les prochaines étapes ; nombres prononcés clairement..
exercices.reponseAttendue: In short, service quality improved markedly over the half-year, but at a cost that was higher than planned. On the positive side, our customer satisfaction score rose from seventy-two to eighty-one, its highest level in three years, and average response time more than halved, falling from nine hours to four. However, I won't sugar-coat the cost side: the department finished twelve per cent over budget. The bulk of that overspend is attributable to temporary staff we brought in during the system migration, so it's very largely a one-off. Now that the migration is complete, those contracts have ended. The underlying point, though, is that part of the improvement in response times came from that extra capacity, so we need to make sure we don't slip back. Looking ahead, we have two priorities: first, to automate the most frequent requests, which should absorb about a fifth of our volume; and second, to monitor response times weekly, so that we can keep satisfaction above eighty while bringing costs back in line with budget by the end of the year.

exercices.consigne:
You are Head of Workplace Services at Corvane Analytics (240 employees). The lease on the company's Lyon office (3,200 m²) expires on 30 September. Six months of badge data show average daily occupancy of 38%, rising to 61% on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Three options are on the table: (A) renew the current lease; (B) move to a smaller flexible workspace of about 1,800 m²; (C) give up the office and go fully remote. Write a recommendation report to the Executive Committee: state the purpose, summarise the findings, assess the three options, make and justify a recommendation, and set out the next steps. Write at least 200 words. — Rappel : la recommandation doit apparaître dès le début ; distinguez les faits de votre interprétation.
200 mots minimum, en 30 minutes.
Critères : Respect du sujet : les trois options sont évaluées et une seule est recommandée. ; Structure en rubriques (purpose, findings, options, recommendation, next steps), recommandation annoncée dès le début. ; Faits chiffrés distingués de l'interprétation (this suggests, in our view). ; Langue de la recommandation maîtrisée : recommend that + base verbale, on balance, provided that, inversion conditionnelle. ; Cohésion : progression logique, reprises par démonstratif + nom (this option, these figures). ; Au moins 200 mots, registre soutenu et lisible, rédigés dans le temps imparti..
exercices.reponseAttendue:
Report: Office Strategy Following the Expiry of the Lyon Lease
To: Executive Committee
From: Hélène Marchetti, Head of Workplace Services

1. Purpose
This report assesses three options for our Lyon premises, whose lease expires on 30 September, and recommends relocating to a smaller flexible workspace.

2. Findings
Badge data collected over the past six months show that average daily occupancy has stabilised at 38%, peaking at 61% on Tuesdays and Thursdays. A staff survey (182 responses) indicates that most employees value two to three office days per week, chiefly for collaboration and onboarding. These figures suggest that our current space is designed for a way of working that no longer exists.

3. Options assessed
Option A, renewing the current lease, offers continuity but would lock us into fixed costs of around €1.1 million a year for space we largely do not use.
Option B, relocating to an 1,800 m² flexible workspace, would cut annual costs by an estimated 34% while still accommodating peak attendance, provided that a desk-booking system is introduced.
Option C, moving to fully remote working, would generate the greatest savings but would, in our view, undermine team cohesion and the integration of the forty graduates we plan to recruit this year.

4. Recommendation
On balance, it is recommended that the committee approve Option B. Not only does it align our footprint with actual usage, but it also preserves the in-person collaboration that staff themselves describe as essential. The main risk lies in overcrowding on peak days; this could be mitigated by a booking system and by staggering team days.

5. Next steps
Should the committee endorse this recommendation, Workplace Services will shortlist three sites by 15 May, present a detailed cost comparison in June and consult staff representatives before any lease is signed.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss these findings at the April meeting.

metier.titre: Cadre européen commun de référence pour les langues (CECRL) et son volume complémentaire
metier.commentaire: Le volume complémentaire du CECRL actualise les descripteurs (médiation, interaction en ligne, compétences plurilingues). Le VTest affine l'échelle en 10 niveaux de A2 à C1.
metier.exploitation: Preuve : descripteurs utilisés dans la grille de positionnement. Action : objectifs de chaque parcours rédigés avec les descripteurs du niveau visé.

metier.titre: Espace candidat VTest – passage du test en ligne
metier.commentaire: Le test se passe en ligne : compréhension orale et écrite adaptatives, expression orale notée automatiquement, rédaction en 30 minutes avec un nombre minimal de mots selon le niveau (80, 150 ou 200 mots).
metier.exploitation: Preuve : description des épreuves reprise dans le livret stagiaire. Action : entraînements chronométrés au format des 4 épreuves en fin de parcours.

metier.titre: Répertoire spécifique : liste des organismes préparant à la certification RS6905
metier.commentaire: La fiche publie la liste des organismes préparant à la certification ; l'organisme vérifie son inscription et les conditions fixées par le certificateur.
metier.exploitation: Preuve : capture de la liste. Action : convention ou accord avec le certificateur tenu à jour dans le dossier qualité.

technologique.titre: Description des niveaux communs de référence du CECRL
technologique.commentaire: Les descripteurs « interaction en ligne » et « médiation » s'appliquent aux réunions à distance et aux échanges écrits instantanés, désormais courants en contexte professionnel.
technologique.exploitation: Preuve : grille d'entraînement à la visioconférence. Action : mises en situation de réunion en ligne intégrées aux classes virtuelles.

technologique.titre: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 – recommandation W3C
technologique.commentaire: Les ressources audio et vidéo de la plateforme doivent être accompagnées de transcriptions et de sous-titres pour rester accessibles.
technologique.exploitation: Preuve : transcriptions disponibles pour chaque dialogue et audio. Action : contrôle de la présence des transcriptions à chaque mise à jour des contenus.
